judged_text: The sync-mode gate omits the userId check that refreshOAuthTokens applies, so minimumTokenResponseSchema is used whenever the env flags are set even when the token was refreshed natively (Salesforce never routes through refreshOAuthTokens at all). On sync-enabled deployments Salesforce refreshes against login.salesforce.com then stores a key stripped to {access_token, refresh_token} — instance_url, signature, scope and token_type are dropped (z.object strips unknown keys), so the next jsforce.Connection is built without an instance URL and Salesforce breaks permanently; team-owned (userId null) Office365 credentials likewise get their rotated refresh_token overwritten with the literal "refresh_token".

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse` the decision to use `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is gated only by `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, with no `userId`/“actually synced” check (unlike `refreshOAuthTokens`, which requires `userId`). This means on sync-enabled deployments even native refresh flows (e.g., Office365 team credentials where `credential.userId` can be null and thus *won’t* route through the sync endpoint) will still be parsed with the minimum schema. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` also forcibly sets `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" when missing, which can overwrite a real stored refresh token during merges like Office365 (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.data) }`). Additionally, Salesforce refresh bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens` entirely but still uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, so the same mismatch can lead to validating/storing an incomplete token shape under sync-mode assumptions.
